subject: general
question: In June 2025, the Government of India planned to shut down the National Polio Surveillance Network (NPSN) established by which international organisation?
solution:
The correct answer is __**World Health Organization**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Polio Surveillance Network (NPSN)** was established in **1997** as a collaborative effort between the **Government of India** and the **World Health Organization (WHO)** to provide technical assistance for polio eradication.
 
• In **June 2025**, the **Government of India** plans to complete the transition of the **NPSN**, effectively shutting down the **WHO**-managed framework to integrate its functions into the national public health system.
 
• The **NPSN** played a pivotal role in the **Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI)**, utilizing a vast network of **Surveillance Medical Officers (SMOs)** to monitor **Acute Flaccid Paralysis (AFP)** cases across the country.
 
• Through the rigorous monitoring and immunization strategies supported by the **WHO**, **India** reported its last case of wild poliovirus in **January 2011** and was officially certified **Polio-free** in **March 2014**.
 
• The transition signifies **India's** capacity to independently manage large-scale **Vaccine Preventable Diseases (VPDs)** surveillance using its own institutional resources and manpower. ***Hence, the correct answer is World Health Organization.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **World Health Organization (WHO):**

 
 
• Established on **7 April 1948**, the **WHO** is a specialized agency of the **United Nations** responsible for international public health.
 
• Headquartered in **Geneva**, **Switzerland**, it works with **194 Member States** to promote health, keep the world safe, and serve the vulnerable.
 
• It provides technical support and sets international health standards, such as those used in the **NPSN** for polio surveillance.
 
 
 
• **Polio Eradication in India:**
 
 
• The last case of wild poliovirus was detected on **13 January 2011**, in a two-year-old girl in **Howrah**, **West Bengal**.
 
• **India** maintained a zero-case record for **three consecutive years**, meeting the **WHO** criteria for eradication.
 
• The **Pulse Polio Programme**, launched in **1995**, was the primary vehicle for administering the **Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV)** to children under the **age** of **5**.
 
 
 
• **Transition and Repurposing:**
 
 
• The infrastructure developed by the **WHO** for polio is now being repurposed to strengthen surveillance for other diseases like **Measles**, **Rubella**, and **Neonatal Tetanus**.
 
• This shift is part of the **National Health Mission (NHM)** strategy to achieve universal immunization coverage across all **states** and **Union Territories**.
 
 
 
• **Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI):**
 
 
• It is a public-private partnership led by national governments and five partners: **WHO**, **Rotary International**, the **US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)**, **UNICEF**, and the **Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Surveillance Mechanism:** The **NPSN** utilized nearly **40,000 reporting units** and over **1,000** specialized staff members to ensure no case of paralysis went unnoticed.
 
• **Polio Vaccines:** India utilizes both **Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV)** for mass campaigns and **Inactivated Polio Vaccine (IPV)** as part of the **Universal Immunization Programme (UIP)**.
 
• **Current Status:** While **India** is polio-free, the risk of importation remains from countries where the virus is still endemic, such as **Pakistan** and **Afghanistan**, necessitating continued vigilance.
